outcome: incidence of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
cohort: Pregnant women diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (n=48)
finding: Active management of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is associated with good perinatal outcomes, despite higher rates of cesarean section, and elevated serum transaminase levels appear to correlate with poor perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was high (41.66%) in the cohort of women with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy managed actively.
